queue.drain()

Waits until every task already in the queue has finished, then resolves. Tasks added while the queue is draining are run too, so the promise settles only when the queue is empty and no worker is busy.

Syntax

await queue.drain({ timeout: 30000, rejectOnError: false });

Options

NameTypeDefaultMeaning
timeoutnumbernoneMilliseconds to wait before rejecting with a timeout error.
rejectOnErrorbooleanfalseReject as soon as one task fails instead of waiting for the rest.
pausebooleanfalseStop taking new tasks while draining, so the queue ends empty.

Example

Drain the queue before the process exits, so a deploy does not cut a task off halfway:

process.on("SIGTERM", async () => {
  await queue.drain({ timeout: 10000, pause: true });
  process.exit(0);
});

If the timeout passes first, the tasks still running are left to finish on their own and the promise rejects with E_DRAIN_TIMEOUT.
